library(tidyverse)

## Part 1: Terra package
Benefits of terra
- **data model**: ...


### 1.1 Read in Data
```{r}
# Read data by terra
dem <- terra::rast(system.file("raster/dem.tif", package = "spDataLarge"))
landsat <- terra::rast(system.file("raster/landsat.tif", package = "spDataLarge"))
srtm <- terra::rast(system.file("raster/srtm.tif", package = "spDataLarge"))
```
### 1.2 Explore elevation at Mt. Mongón, Perú
1. Make a boxplot and histogram of elevation at Mt. Mongón, Perú
2. Reclassify dem and compute the mean for the three classes:
    - Low, where elevation is less than 300 
    - Medium
    - High, where elevation is greater than 500

1.2.1 Make a boxplot and histogram
```{r}
# Use terra:: so R uses terra's version
# Terra histagram
terra::hist(dem,
    main = "Digital Elevation Model Distribution",
    xlab = "Value"
)

# Terra boxplot
terra::boxplot(dem,
    main = "Digital Elevation Model Distribution",
    ylab = "Value"
)
```

1.2 Reclassify and group
```{r}
# terra method
# Each row is one rule: from, to, new value
rcl <- matrix(c(-Inf, 300, 0,  # Low
                 300, 500, 1,  # Medium
                 500, Inf, 2), # High
             ncol = 3, byrow = TRUE
             )

# Apply the matrix to reclassify the raster, making all cells 0 or 1 or 2
dem_rcl <- terra::classify(dem, rcl = rcl)

# Assign labels to the numerical categories
# A plain data.frame works with both older and newer terra
levels(dem_rcl) <- data.frame(id = 0:2,
                              cats = c("low", "medium", "high"))

# Calculate mean elevation for each category using original DEM values
elevation_mean <- terra::zonal(dem, dem_rcl, fun = "mean")
elevation_mean
```

```{r}
plot(dem_rcl)
```

### 3. Compare NDVI and NDWI for Zion National Park
```{r}
scale_factor <- 0.0000275
offset <- 0.2

scale_function <- function(x) {
  x * scale_factor + offset
}

landsat_scaled <- terra::app(landsat, fun = scale_function)
```

```{r}
ndwi_fun <- function(green, nir){
    (green - nir)/(green + nir)
}

ndvi_fun <- function(nir, red){
  (nir - red)/(nir + red)
}
```

```{r}
ndwi_rast <- terra::lapp(landsat_scaled[[c(2, 4)]],
                         fun = ndwi_fun)

ndvi_rast <- terra::lapp(landsat_scaled[[c(4, 3)]],
                         fun = ndvi_fun)
```

```{r}
plot(ndwi_rast,
     main = "Zion National Park NDWI")
```


```{r}
combine <- c(ndvi_rast, ndwi_rast) # Stack rasters

plot(combine, main = c("NDVI", "NDWI")) # Plot
```

## Part 2: Stars package

1.1 Read in data
```{r}
# Read data using stars package
dem_s <- stars::read_stars(system.file("raster/dem.tif", package = "spDataLarge"))
landsat_s <- stars::read_stars(system.file("raster/landsat.tif", package = "spDataLarge"))
srtm_s <- stars::read_stars(system.file("raster/srtm.tif", package = "spDataLarge"))
```

1.2 Explore Mt. 
```{r}
# Stars histagram
dem_values <- as.vector(dem_s[[1]])

hist(dem_values,
    main = "Digital Elevation Model Distribution",
    xlab = "Value"
)

boxplot(dem_values, 
    main = "Digital Elevation Model Distribution",
    ylab = "Value"
)
```

```{r}
# Stars method
dem_rcl <- cut(dem_s,
               breaks = c(-Inf, 300, 500, Inf),
               labels = c("low", "medium", "high")
              )

elevation_mean <- tibble(
    elevation = as.vector(dem[[1]]),
    cats = factor(as.vector(dem_rcl[[1]]),
    levels = levels(dem_rcl[[1]]))) |> 
    group_by(cats) |> 
    summarize(mean_elevation = 
        mean(elevation, na.rm = TRUE))

elevation_mean
```

```{r}
tm_shape(dem_rcl) +
    tm_raster()
```

```{r}
# Polygonize the reclassified raster, merging cells of the same class
dem_polys <- sf::st_as_sf(dem_rcl, merge = TRUE) |> 
  group_by(dem.tif) |> 
  summarise() # Dissolve into one (multi)polygon per class

# Compute the mean of DEM values falling inside each polygon
aggregate(dem, by = dem_polys, FUN = mean) |> 
  sf::st_as_sf() |> 
  mutate(cats = dem_polys$dem.tif)
```
